title: Paperclip and the Gehlen network as a homecoming; Nazi Germany as a field laboratory

tellings.quote: that in a lot of ways both paperclip and the absorption of the Galen network were a homecoming. It's almost as if Nazi Germany was set up as a field laboratory to do some highly unethical things.

plain: Nazi Germany may have been set up as a kind of field laboratory for "highly unethical" experiments, so that bringing its people to America afterward was really a homecoming. The writer Jason Jorjani offers this theory to Michels without naming a source. He points to Paperclip, the US programme that brought German scientists over after the war, and to the absorption of the Gehlen network, the German spy ring of General Reinhard Gehlen that US intelligence took over, and says both were "in a lot of ways" a homecoming.
